gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per RMS watt: the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT works out to about $1.70 per RMS watt ($149.99 / 88 W) and the JVC KD-T920BTS to about $2.03 ($179.00 / 88 W). Neither states that the Pioneer's 4 V pre-outs give about 6 dB more signal into an add-on amp than the Sony MEX-N5300BT's 2 V pre-outs.
standout_why: I opened three pages: the Abt DEH-S4220BT page (ranked result 6 in chat 1 and the source of the $149.99 card), the World Wide Stereo 2026 guide (rank 9 in chat 2) and the Sonic Electronix DEH-S4220BT page (rank 14). Abt already states the 4 V x 2-pair pre-outs and 'MOSFET 50W x 4', but gives no RMS figure and no cost per watt. World Wide Stereo names the Sony MEX-N5300BT as Best Value Single-DIN but lists no RMS or pre-out figures. Sonic Electronix already states 22 W RMS x 4 and 1.5 A USB for the Pioneer. So the raw inputs are partly on rival pages, but none works out $ per RMS watt or the dB gap between pre-out voltages. Crutchfield's 2026 guide, the only cited page, returned 403, so I could not check it. It may list RMS ratings.
decides: This backs the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT as the value pick over the JVC KD-T920BTS. It has the same 88 W total RMS, as rated by Sonic Electronix, for $29 less. That is $1.70 per RMS watt against $2.03. It also has the highest pre-out voltage (4 V vs JVC 2.5 V vs Sony 2 V) and 7.5 W USB charging against the Sony's 5 W, which matters to anyone planning to add an amplifier or charge a phone from the head unit. There is a caveat: pioneerofficial.com rates the Pioneer at only 14 W RMS x 4 under CTA-2006. On that rating the cost is $2.68 per watt, and the JVC wins on cost per watt. Settle the conflict on usa.pioneer before publishing.
